name: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine (T-DM1)
histology: invasive breast carcinoma (histology-agnostic; includes invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) and invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC))

biomarkers.note: HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate (trastuzumab linked to emtansine, a microtubule inhibitor): requires HER2-positive disease (IHC 3+ or ISH-amplified). Per DeVita 12th ed. and Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Invasive Breast Cancer.

lineOfTherapy: second-line and beyond for HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane); may be considered in the second line if not a candidate for fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan; optimal third-line-and-beyond sequence not established

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: prior trastuzumab and taxane chemotherapy (metastatic use)

drugs.name: Ado-trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1)

provenance.locator: lines 20796 to 20802 (drug table: ado-trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg IV every 3 wk, HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer); line 21438 (dosed at 3.6 mg/kg IV every 21 days)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., ado-trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks (every 21 days) for HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (lines 20796 to 20802; 21438). Concordant with Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v6.2026 metastatic dosing (T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV day 1, every 21 days, BINV-Q 10 of 15). Do not confuse with fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan; do not substitute trastuzumab and hyaluronidase-oysk for this agent.

supportiveCare: Antiemetics: low-to-moderate emetic risk; prophylaxis per emetogenicity tier.
Cardiac: evaluate LVEF before and during HER2-targeted therapy (BINV-M 1 of 10).
Monitor platelets (thrombocytopenia) and hepatic transaminases (transaminitis) each cycle per DeVita adverse-event profile (line 21439).

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3 to 4 thrombocytopenia or significant transaminase elevation
doseModificationRules.text: Hold or dose-reduce per labeling for thrombocytopenia or hepatotoxicity; obtain clinical review. DeVita reports thrombocytopenia 12.8% and transient transaminitis 4.3% (line 21439).

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: lines 20796 to 20802 (drug table dose 3.6 mg/kg IV every 3 wk, HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer); lines 21432 to 21439 (EMILIA-context approval, dosed 3.6 mg/kg IV every 21 days, toxicity profile)

guideline.locator: Dosing: Cytotoxic Regimens for Recurrent/Stage IV Disease, HER2-Positive, T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV day 1 every 21 days, BINV-Q 10 of 15; line placement (second/third line and beyond) BINV-Q 3 of 15 and footnote r; adjuvant use for residual disease 3.6 mg/kg every 21 days for 14 cycles BINV-M 7 of 10

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for the HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate ado-trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1). Serves subtype #4 (HER2-positive) metastatic breast cancer, histology-agnostic across invasive ductal (#1) and invasive lobular (#2) carcinoma. The dose is grounded in DeVita 12th ed. (core): 3.6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks / every 21 days for HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (lines 20796 to 20802 and 21438), concordant with Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v6.2026 metastatic dosing (BINV-Q 10 of 15). Modeled as the metastatic use (cycles null, continue until progression); the same 3.6 mg/kg every-21-day dose is used adjuvantly for 14 cycles in residual HER2-positive disease per the guideline (noted, not the modeled setting). CAUTION recorded in provenance: DeVita states 6.4 mg/m2 for trastuzumab deruxtecan in the gastric setting (line 99219); that is a different drug and a different setting and must never be applied to T-DM1 or to breast dosing. No field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
